unit.sep: Observe,model,investigate controls,calculate rates and communicate conditional conclusions.
unit.careers: Illustrative plant-research/environmental communication practices;no agronomic dose prescription or laboratory qualification.
unit.focus: Root water/mineral absorption,xylem cohesion/tension,source-sink phloem,actual safe environmental/structural mass-loss investigations and balanced plant-life implications.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional garden report says fertiliser is sugar food,phloem only flows down and a water-uptake bubble directly measures evaporation.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Approved root observations,water/ion gradients,source/sink changes,attributed research context,actual mass-loss records,separate fictional data and conditional awareness messages.
unit.drivingQuestion: How do transport mechanisms and controlled evidence support plant-life decisions? KICD: Why is transport in plants important?
unit.storylineThread: Root → water/ions → cohesion/tension → phloem → evidence → plan → airflow → leafarea → rates/benefits → awareness → audit → independent explanation.
unit.content: Absorption of Water and Mineral Salts; Translocation; Factors affecting transpiration; Importance of transpiration
unit.coreCompetencies:
Citizenship: as the learner sensitises the community on the importance of watering and manuring plants to sustain plant growth.
Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on experiments on factors affecting transpiration in plants.
unit.values:
Unity: as the learner engages in assigned roles while working with others in the process of investigation of factors affecting transpiration.
Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on the importance of watering and manuring plants to sustain plant growth.
unit.pcis:
Safety and security: as the learner observes safety precautions while carrying out experiments in groups to investigate factors affecting transpiration in plants.
Environmental issues: as the learner creates awareness in the community on the use of fertilisers (Di-ammonium Phosphate, Calcium Ammonium Nitrate, Urea) in boosting crop production.

No teaching cards,practical equipment,peers,hints or media. Data are fictional. Written interpretation does not certify actual outcome c investigation,digital viewing or community sharing.

sections.title: 1. Absorption and xylem mechanism
sections.prompt: Draw a labelled soil→root→xylem→leaf→air pathway. Explain water entry,selective mineral-ion uptake,and root-hair function. Explain cohesion,adhesion and transpiration pull;give a reason very concentrated soil solution can reduce water uptake. Distinguish mineral nutrients from sugar food.
sections.exemplar: Water crosses selectively permeable membranes down water potential;ion transport selective and may need energy against gradient,not osmosis. Root hairs increase absorbing contact area. Evaporation/vapour loss creates tension transmitted through cohesive water with wall adhesion;capillarity alone incomplete for tallplants. Concentrated soil lowers water potential and may reduce/reverse entry. Mineral ions are nutrients,not photosynthate sugars.

sections.title: 2. Source,sink and route evidence
sections.prompt: Explain both PT12FinalBsource/sink examples with labelled phloem arrows. Include sugar/water and pressure roles,and explain why direction need not always be downward. State why coloured water in a stem does not establish sugar translocation and identify one control needed in a tracer-path study.
sections.exemplar: Storageorgansource→sprout sink before effective leafphotosynthesis;latermatureleafsource→growingrootsink. Phloem translocates organic solutes in water source-to-sink with pressure gradients and loading/unloading roles;differentroutes can pointdifferentdirections. Dyedwaterrouteisnotproofsugarinphloem. Accept sham/healthy/source-equivalence control and acknowledge injuryconfounds.

sections.title: 3. Interpret and design an investigation
sections.prompt: For FinalA,calculate each condition’s mean background-corrected mass loss and g/min rate. Compare them and state a justified conclusion and limitation. Name independent/dependent variables,two controls and a repeat/check. Propose a separate structural leaf-area comparison and one confound. Explain why a bubble potometer’s displacement is an uptake proxy and why this written record does not certify performed investigation.

sections.title: 4. Explain a benefit with a limit
sections.prompt: Explain one specific way transpiration/transport supports plant life and one risk of excessive water loss. Give a useful watering/nutrient-awareness message with a condition or environmental limit. State one separate action observation needed before claiming actual community engagement.
